1.name: Metasedimentary and metavolcanic rocks
1.lithology: Major: amphibolite, hornblende gneiss, biotite gneiss; Minor: quartzite, banded iron formation, metaconglomerate, marble, pelitic schist
1.description: Amphibolite, hornblende gneiss, biotite gneiss, quartzite, iron-formation, metaconglomerate, marble, and pelitic schist; locally preserved textures and structures suggest origin to be sedimentary or volcanic. Older than 2,875 Ma in Teton Range; older than 3,200 Ma in Granite Mountains; older than 2,600 Ma in Medicine Bow Mountains and Sierra Madre, where it is the Late Archean Phantom Lake Metamorphic Suite 3.
1.reference: Green, Gregory N., and Drouillard, Patricia H., 1994, The Digital Geologic Map of Wyoming in ARC/INFO Format: U.S. Geological Survey Open-File Report 94-0425, scale 1:500,000.

2.name: Glacial deposits
2.description: Till and outwash of sand, gravel, and boulders.
2.reference: Green, Gregory N., and Drouillard, Patricia H., 1994, The Digital Geologic Map of Wyoming in ARC/INFO Format: U.S. Geological Survey Open-File Report 94-0425, scale 1:500,000.

3.name: Gravel, pediment, and fan deposits
3.description: Mostly locally derived clasts.  Includes some glacial deposits along east flank of Wind River Range. Locally includes some Tertiary gravels.
3.reference: Green, Gregory N., and Drouillard, Patricia H., 1994, The Digital Geologic Map of Wyoming in ARC/INFO Format: U.S. Geological Survey Open-File Report 94-0425, scale 1:500,000.

4.name: Granitic rocks of 2,600-Ma Age Group
4.lithology: Major: granite; Minor: granodiorite, amphibolite, quartz monzonite; Incidental: metasedimentary
4.description: Teton Range--Mount Owen Quartz Monzonite.  Age 2,500+/- Ma; may be of Early Proterozoic age.  Gros Ventre and Washakie Ranges--Granitic rocks.  Yellowstone National Park, Owl Creek, Granite, and Seminoe Mountains, Rawlins uplift, and Medicine Bow Mountains--Granite.  Wind River Range--Granodiorite to porphyritic and equigranular granite.  Sierra Madre--Granite and granodiorite.  Laramie Mountains--Granite, amphibolite, and minor amounts of metasedimentary rocks.  Hartville uplift--Granite and quartz monzonite.  Black Hills uplift--Granite and minor amounts of metasedimentary rocks.
4.reference: Green, Gregory N., and Drouillard, Patricia H., 1994, The Digital Geologic Map of Wyoming in ARC/INFO Format: U.S. Geological Survey Open-File Report 94-0425, scale 1:500,000.

5.name: water
5.reference: Green, Gregory N., and Drouillard, Patricia H., 1994, The Digital Geologic Map of Wyoming in ARC/INFO Format: U.S. Geological Survey Open-File Report 94-0425, scale 1:500,000.

6.name: Landslide deposits
6.description: Locally includes intermixed landslide and glacial deposits, talus, and rock-glacier deposits.
6.reference: Green, Gregory N., and Drouillard, Patricia H., 1994, The Digital Geologic Map of Wyoming in ARC/INFO Format: U.S. Geological Survey Open-File Report 94-0425, scale 1:500,000.

7.name: Alluvium and Colluvium
7.lithology: Major: clay, silt, sand; Minor: gravel
7.description: Clay, silt, sand, and gravel in flood plains, fans, terraces, and slopes.
7.reference: Green, Gregory N., and Drouillard, Patricia H., 1994, The Digital Geologic Map of Wyoming in ARC/INFO Format: U.S. Geological Survey Open-File Report 94-0425, scale 1:500,000.

rule_notes: first match over major lithologies, then name, then description; volcanic with bottom age >= 145.0 Ma -> greenstone_metavolcanic; clastic sedimentary with bottom age <= 2.58 Ma -> alluvium; 'water' -> other
